bug_description.original: Detailed report: https://oss-fuzz.com/testcase?key=5742300546727936 Project: open62541 Fuzzer: afl_open62541_fuzz_binary_message Crash Type: Heap-use-after-free READ 8 Crash State: UA_WorkQueue_cleanup UA_Server_delete fuzz_binary_message.cc Sanitizer: address (ASAN)
bug_description.normalized: The saved witness creates two sessions, not one. After the first `CreateSessionRequest`, the fuzzing-only helper at `ua_server_binary.c:465,472-474` rewrites the later `AddNodesRequest` header with that first session's authentication token, and `processMSG`'s request-local lookup at `ua_server_binary.c:478-480` resolves the request to the still-inactive first session and removes it through the `sessionRequired && !session->activated` path, queuing delayed callback `C1`. The witness later creates a second session; the helper overwrites the saved token with that second session's token, and each later `ActivateSessionRequest`, `CreateSubscriptionRequest`, and `CloseSessionRequest` separately rewrites `requestHeader->authenticationToken` and performs a fresh session lookup that re-materializes session2. `ActivateSession` marks session2 active, `CreateSubscription` links a subscription to it, and `CloseSession` queues delayed callback `C2`, so shutdown starts with delayed queue `[C2, C1]`. During the first `UA_WorkQueue_cleanup` pass from `UA_Server_run_shutdown`, executing `C2` calls `UA_Session_deleteMembersCleanup`, which still deletes the second session's attached subscription and inserts the subscription free `S` at the queue head. The queue walk then advances to the precomputed iterator `C1` but removes `S`, frees `C1` while it remains linked, and the second `UA_WorkQueue_cleanup` pass from `UA_Server_delete` rereads that freed first-session callback and triggers the ASAN heap-use-after-free read.

sink.description: During the second `UA_WorkQueue_cleanup` pass from `UA_Server_delete`, the delayed-callback iterator dereferences the already freed first-session callback `C1`, which remained linked after the first cleanup pass freed its containing 368-byte `session_list_entry`.

root_cause.description: Delayed session cleanup still tears down attached subscriptions from inside `UA_Session_deleteMembersCleanup`. In the saved witness this runs for the second, subscribed session callback `C2`, and `UA_Session_deleteSubscription` inserts `sub->delayedFreePointers` onto the same delayed-callback queue that `UA_WorkQueue_manuallyProcessDelayed` is already draining. The fix moves subscription and queued publish-response cleanup out of `UA_Session_deleteMembersCleanup` and performs it earlier in `removeSession` before the session itself is scheduled as delayed work.

fine_trace.code: retval = UA_decodeBinary(msg, &offset, request, requestType, server->config.customDataTypesSize, server->config.customDataTypes);
fine_trace.note: Materializes the typed OPC UA requests from attacker bytes. Along the vulnerability-relevant path, the saved witness decodes a first `CreateSessionRequest`, an `AddNodesRequest`, a second `CreateSessionRequest`, an `ActivateSessionRequest`, a `CreateSubscriptionRequest`, and a `CloseSessionRequest`.

The first decoded `CreateSessionRequest` allocates the first heap `session_list_entry` (`sentry1`). This object embeds the later delayed callback `cleanupCallback` at the start of the same 368-byte allocation and is the session that will be removed by the later non-activated `AddNodes` path.
After the first `CreateSessionRequest`, the fuzzing-only helper copies `sentry1`'s returned authentication token into the global `unsafe_fuzz_authenticationToken`.
When the later `AddNodesRequest` is decoded, the same fuzzing helper overwrites that request header's authentication token with the saved token from step 4.

The session-lookup block at lines 478-480 resolves the injected token from step 5 to the first live session pointer. The later `!session->activated` branch proves this lookup produced a non-null `session` for the saved witness, whether it came from the channel list or the session-manager fallback.
`AddNodesRequest` is a session-required service, and the first session from step 6 was created but never activated. This non-activated-session branch is therefore taken on that first session.

The `UA_SessionManager_removeSession` call from step 7 queues the first session's delayed cleanup callback (`C1`). Because `UA_WorkQueue_enqueueDelayed` inserts at the head, `C1` is now the only node on `server->workQueue.delayedCallbacks`.
The later second `CreateSessionRequest` allocates a distinct second `session_list_entry` (`sentry2`). This is the session that will later be activated, subscribed, and closed.

After the second `CreateSessionRequest`, the fuzzing helper overwrites the global `unsafe_fuzz_authenticationToken` with the second session's authentication token, replacing the first session token from step 4.
When the saved witness reaches the later `ActivateSessionRequest`, the helper copies the second session token from step 10 into that request header.

The same lookup block at lines 478-480 resolves the token from step 11 to the second session pointer. The later `ActivateSession` call proves this lookup produced a non-null `session` for the saved witness.

`Service_ActivateSession` flips the second session into the activated state. That state transition is required before the later session-required `CreateSubscriptionRequest` and `CloseSessionRequest` can each survive their own request-local `!session->activated` check instead of taking the removal path from step 7.
When the later `CreateSubscriptionRequest` is decoded, lines 472-474 first clear any decoded authentication token and then copy the saved second-session token from step 10 into this request header.
The per-request session lookup at lines 478-480 resolves the rewritten `CreateSubscriptionRequest` token from step 14 back to the second session pointer.

Because step 13 already activated session2, the later `CreateSubscriptionRequest` survives the request-local non-activated check and runs on the session pointer re-materialized at step 15. It allocates `sub2`, and `UA_Session_addSubscription` links `sub2` into `session2->serverSubscriptions`; the subscription object begins with its own delayed-callback node `delayedFreePointers`.
When the later `CloseSessionRequest` is decoded, lines 472-474 again clear any decoded authentication token and copy the saved second-session token into that request header.

The per-request lookup at lines 478-480 resolves the rewritten `CloseSessionRequest` token from step 17 back to the second session pointer, so this request also reaches `Service_CloseSession` on session2 instead of the non-activated-session removal path.

`Service_CloseSession` calls `UA_SessionManager_removeSession` for the second session and queues its delayed cleanup callback (`C2`). Head insertion puts `C2` in front of the already queued first-session callback from step 8, so the shutdown queue is `[C2, C1]` before delayed work starts draining.

During the first `UA_WorkQueue_cleanup` pass from `UA_Server_run_shutdown`, the queue head `C2` runs `UA_Session_deleteMembersCleanup` for the second session. Because that session still owns `sub2`, this loop deletes the subscription inside the delayed callback, and `UA_Session_deleteSubscription` immediately enqueues `sub2->delayedFreePointers` (`S`) at the head of the same `delayedCallbacks` list. The fix moves this subscription cleanup into `removeSession` before the session callback is enqueued.

`UA_WorkQueue_manuallyProcessDelayed` had already cached `C1` as the next iterator before step 20 inserted `S` at the head. On the next loop iteration, `dc` still advances to the old first-session callback `C1`, but `SIMPLEQ_REMOVE_HEAD` now dequeues `S` instead. The iterator and the queue head are therefore no longer talking about the same node.

Because step 21 removed `S` instead of `C1`, the loop still executes `dc == C1` and frees the first session's `session_list_entry` while that same `cleanupCallback` remains linked as the queue head. ASAN's free stack points to this free during the first cleanup pass from `UA_Server_run_shutdown`.

depends_on.via: dc == C1 while queue head stayed linked

fine_trace.note: `LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput` calls `UA_Server_delete(server)` immediately after `UA_Server_run_shutdown(server)` (`fuzz_binary_message.cc`:36-37), so `UA_WorkQueue_cleanup` runs a second time. That second pass iterates `delayedCallbacks` again, rereads the freed first-session callback left linked by step 22, and ASAN reports the 8-byte heap-use-after-free read at the start of the freed `session_list_entry`.

free_context.description: The freed first-session callback node is released during the first cleanup pass reached from `UA_Server_run_shutdown`.

allocation_context.description: The stale callback is the `cleanupCallback` field at the start of a heap `session_list_entry` allocated for the first `CreateSessionRequest`; the saved message order and queue mutation make that first session callback the freed-but-still-linked node reread later.

format.name: OPC UA Binary/TCP message sequence
format.contract: The staged 1404-byte witness is a raw OPC UA Binary/TCP conversation with `HELF`, `OPNF`, and then nine `MSGF` chunks whose first request-type NodeIds statically decode, in order, as `ns=32;i=8224`, `CreateSessionRequest`, `ns=32;i=8224`, `AddNodesRequest`, `CreateSessionRequest`, `ActivateSessionRequest`, `ns=32;i=8224`, `CreateSubscriptionRequest`, and `CloseSessionRequest`. With the fuzzing-build authentication-token copy at `ua_server_binary.c:465,472-474`, the `AddNodesRequest` header is rewritten to the first session token, while the later `ActivateSessionRequest`, `CreateSubscriptionRequest`, and `CloseSessionRequest` headers are each separately rewritten to the second session token and each re-resolved through `processMSG`'s lookup at `ua_server_binary.c:478-480`. That exact order first queues cleanup for an unactivated first session and later creates, activates, subscribes, and closes a second session, so shutdown drains `[C2, C1]`, inserts a subscription free at the queue head, and only then crashes on the second cleanup pass.
